assessment_metadata.title: Brain2Qwerty Public-Evidence Pilot Assessment v4.1.3
assessment_metadata.assessment_purpose: Determine the strongest defensible Brain2Qwerty capability claim, separate neural-signal contribution from language-model and task priors, resolve exact v1/v2 configurations, and establish prohibited thought-decoding, clinical, and deployment inferences.

assessors.name_or_role: UNESCO NeuroAI public-evidence pilot assessment process
assessors.responsibility: Public-source extraction, claim adjudication, requirement mapping, and bounded decision preparation
assessors.source_or_basis: v4.1.2 instrument and v4.1.3 controlled source freeze

assessment_metadata.public_private_state: PUBLIC EVIDENCE WITH CONTROLLED PRIVATE GAP REGISTER

limitations: Public-source assessment only.

system_profile.system_name: Brain2Qwerty v2 asynchronous non-invasive MEG-to-text research system
system_profile.system_family: Non-invasive participant-specific neural-to-text research system with generative language-model reconstruction
system_profile.configuration_effective_period: Paper state dated 2026-06-29 through evidence cutoff 2026-07-28

components.name: MEGIN whole-head cryogenic MEG system
components.dependency: Laboratory-scale neural acquisition at 1 kHz; 0.1–330 Hz online filters

components.name: Custom MR-compatible QWERTY keyboard
components.dependency: Overt typing task and training labels

components.name: EnglishBCBL acquisition and preprocessing pipeline
components.version: Paper-described v2 pipeline; public dataset embargoed
components.dependency: 9 participants, 90 sessions, deterministic text-hash 80/10/10 split, 0.5–45 Hz preprocessing

components.name: ConvConformer CTC encoder
components.version: Paper-described and partially code-specified v2 encoder
components.dependency: Participant-specific channel merger, character sequence and neural embeddings

components.name: Word-level SigLIP aligner and CTC tokenizer
components.dependency: Segments neural embeddings at predicted spaces and aligns them to LLM word embeddings

components.name: Neuro-conditioned language model
components.version: Paper best: Qwen3-4B, per-subject LoRA then model soup, rank 128; released default: TinyLlama-1.1B, all-subject LoRA rank 2
components.effective_period: Paper and code states frozen separately
components.dependency: Autoregressive reconstruction from CTC text and MEG-derived word tokens

components.name: Sentence stimulus corpus
components.version: 2,560 selected sentences plus pilot additions; initial pool generated with Llama 4
components.dependency: Constrained experimental target distribution and language prior

components.name: Public Brain2Qwerty repository
components.dependency: Implementation access under CC BY-NC 4.0; data and paper-best checkpoint absent

sc_01.rationale: Whole-head MEG records extracranial magnetic fields without implantation.

sc_02.rationale: Records MEG and infers typed sentence text; no stimulation or actuation.

sc_03.rationale: Exact demonstrated state is research measurement; communication is an aspirational function, not validated clinical use.

sc_04.rationale: MEG is neural-recording data; sentence output is a model-derived reconstruction shaped by motor and language priors.

sc_05.rationale: CTC prediction is followed by an autoregressive LLM.

sc_06.rationale: Acquisition is session-based; neural data, trained models, and outputs may persist.

sc_07.rationale: Recording can cease without implanted hardware; persistence of data/model representations is separately governed.

sc_08.rationale: Researcher-operated acquisition with automated offline decoding.

sc_09.rationale: No clinical, home, consumer, workplace, or other deployment was demonstrated.

sc_10.rationale: Nine healthy adults, 23–56 years, selected for skilled typing.

sc_11.rationale: Healthy-volunteer research prototype with preprint evidence and no clinical validation.

sc_12.rationale: Current evaluation is offline; depends on MEGIN hardware and third-party LLM model family.

intended_uses: Bounded scientific evaluation of participant-specific MEG-to-text reconstruction during overt typing.
Methodological research on asynchronous neural decoding and signal-versus-prior decomposition.
excluded_uses: Clinical diagnosis, therapy, assistive deployment, or patient benefit.
Consumer, workplace, education, justice, defence, or surveillance use.
populations: Studied: nine healthy native-English adults, right-handed skilled typists, ages 23–56, no self-reported neurological or psychiatric conditions.
Excluded from supported claims: patients, children, non-English speakers, people unable to type, diverse disability groups, and general populations.
contexts: BCBL laboratory research in Spain using delayed listen-wait-type trials and whole-head cryogenic MEG.

claim_register.claim_text: Brain2Qwerty v2 can decode natural sentences solely from real-time MEG recordings.

claimed_scope.observation_window: Entire sentence window; output after sentence completion

claim_register.strongest_supported_claim: The reported system decodes previously heard sentences from continuous MEG collected during overt typing without using individual keypress timestamps at inference; it is non-causal, sentence-level, and slow-latency.
prohibited_inferences: Low-latency causal operation
Silent speech or private thought decoding
Patient communication
limitations: “Real-time” describes asynchronous processing without keypress alignment, not incremental causal decoding.
required_evidence_to_change_status: Causal streaming evaluation with measured end-to-end latency and prospective task boundaries.

Patient performance
Unseen-task or naturalistic generalization

claim_register.claim_text: MEG-derived Neuro Tokens contribute information beyond correction from the language model prior.

claimed_scope.endpoint: CER, WER, SemER with and without Neuro Tokens

claim_register.strongest_supported_claim: In the reported ablation, adding MEG-derived Neuro Tokens improved WER from 0.49 to 0.43 and improved CER and SemER relative to the same LLM conditioned only on CTC text.

Independence from motor execution
Independence from sentence or language priors

evidence_register.title: Accurate Decoding of Natural Sentences from Non-Invasive Brain Recordings
evidence_register.population: 9 healthy native-English adults; right-handed proficient typists
evidence_register.function: Decode previously heard sentences during overt keyboard typing from continuous whole-sentence MEG
evidence_register.endpoint: CER, WER, SemER; ablations; participant and sensor analyses
evidence_register.observation_window: 10 approximately one-hour MEG sessions per participant; 90 sessions total
evidence_register.controls_or_comparators: Encoder only; Encoder plus 9-gram; no-Neuro-Token LLM ablation; model-size and sensor-count analyses
evidence_register.result_or_record_content: Mean WER 0.39 ± 0.04; mean SemER 0.059 ± 0.005; mean CER 0.31 ± 0.03; best-participant WER 0.22. Neuro-Token ablation using Qwen3-0.6B changes WER 0.49 to 0.43.
evidence_register.publication_or_record_state: Public preprint dated 29 June 2026; under review
evidence_register.source_retrieval_state: Exact PDF preserved locally and hashed
evidence_register.strongest_supported_claim: Participant-specific asynchronous decoding of overtly typed, previously heard English sentences from continuous MEG was demonstrated under the reported protocol.
prohibited_inferences: Unrestricted thought decoding
Silent-speech decoding
Patient communication utility
Causal low-latency real-time operation
Clinical or consumer readiness
limitations: Preprint has not completed peer review.
No public raw v2 dataset, trained checkpoint, or fully matching executable configuration was available at the evidence cutoff.
The task contains overt motor execution and sentence-specific language priors.

scope.population: Nine healthy native-English adult skilled typists, ages 23–56
scope.context: BCBL laboratory delayed-listen-and-overt-type research task using cryogenic 306-channel MEG
scope.function: Participant-specific asynchronous whole-sentence reconstruction from continuous MEG during overt typing
scope.jurisdiction: Spain research context with global public-claim analysis

legacy_bounded_decision.strongest_supported_claim: Under the reported laboratory protocol, a participant-specific Brain2Qwerty v2 system reconstructed previously heard English sentences from continuous whole-sentence MEG recorded during overt typing. The paper reports mean WER 0.39 ± 0.04 and best-participant WER 0.22. A matched ablation indicates that MEG-derived Neuro Tokens improve WER beyond a CTC-text-only LLM condition, while the system remains materially dependent on overt motor activity, participant-specific data, a constrained sentence distribution, and a generative language prior.
prohibited_inferences: Unrestricted thought reading or private-inner-speech decoding.
Silent-speech, attempted-movement, or patient communication capability.
Causal low-latency real-time operation.
Clinical effectiveness, safety, regulatory authorization, or consumer readiness.
Cross-participant, cross-language, cross-device, or naturalistic-task generalization.
Independent reproduction of the paper-best result from the public release.
Absence of privacy, cybersecurity, equity, or dual-use risk.
participant_conditions_and_dissent: Written informed consent, compensation, ethics approval, and de-identification are reported.
The full consent, withdrawal, participant-governance, data-reuse, and dissent records were not publicly appraised.
jurisdictional_conflicts: No deployment jurisdiction was assessed. Any clinical, consumer, workplace, education, justice, defence, or cross-border data use requires a new jurisdiction-specific assessment.
residual_risks: Fluent but semantically incorrect output may be mistaken for faithful reconstruction.
Public language can collapse overt motor decoding into thought-reading interpretations.
